text: Accessible Public Participation: The business shall support equitable completion of released public tasks without staff credentials or unnecessary barriers.
Persona-Specific Efficiency: The product shall reduce redundant data entry and repeated interactions while preserving clarity.
Mission Coordination: The business shall track requests from intake to documented operational completion and administrative closure.
Personnel Capacity: The business shall maintain recorded skills, availability, and assignments without silent conflicts.
Trustworthy Damage Data: The business shall distinguish self-reported, reviewed, and verified property information.
Operational Accountability: The business shall retain attributable change and decision history.
Timely Follow-Up: The business shall manage durable update obligations and approved escalation.
Reliable Reporting: The business shall use consistent metric definitions and reproducible official reports.
Useful Recovery Information: The business shall publish approved, current, accessible assistance resources.
Controlled Access And Privacy: The business shall limit actions and information by role, record scope, and need.
Appropriate Identification: The business shall distinguish issued identification from verified credentials and actual physical printing.
Partner Coordination: The business shall maintain verified contacts and evidence of approved communication attempts.
Global Ai Action Execution: The product shall provide short-key/shorthand and natural-language action execution from anywhere in supported application contexts.
Safe Optional Ai: The business shall retain human control, factual provenance, and non-AI completion.
Reliability And Recovery: The product shall acknowledge only persisted results and handle interruption without data loss or duplicate effects.
Controlled Configuration And Change: The business shall govern settings, operational definitions, shared commands, and releases.
Emergency Request Through Closure: Trigger: authorized staff records a response request.
Public Report Through Verified Assessment: Trigger: public user reports observed damage.
Responder Onboarding And Deployment: Trigger: personnel coordinator creates or activates a roster record.
Shift Handoff And Official Briefing: Trigger: reporting period ends or authorized staff requests a briefing.
Global Command Execution: Trigger: user invokes context window by shortcut or accessible control.
Source and verification are separate: public observations are not staff findings.

text: Authorization: The system shall authorize each read/write/export/action on the server by user, responsibility, record scope, and field sensitivity. It shall recheck authorization when a prepared action executes.
Public Boundaries: The system shall permit unauthenticated reporting and published-resource access while preventing private-record enumeration and unauthorized retrieval.
Audit: The system shall preserve attributable action/decision records with timestamps, target references, meaningful changes, and applicable execution identifiers.
Save Semantics: The system shall distinguish unsent, sending, persisted, queued, delivered, and failed states as applicable. It shall never label unsaved work as received.
Concurrency: The system shall reject or reconcile stale writes using record versions or an equivalent check. Conflicts shall retain input and show relevant changes.
Idempotency: The system shall prevent duplicate effects for retried submissions and actions using scoped execution identifiers and consistent results.
Error Recovery: The system shall preserve valid input, explain errors, and offer safe retry/cancel options. Non-idempotent external effects shall not be blindly retried.

Time And Unknown Values: The system shall store timestamps consistently and display/report in an approved timezone. Unknown and not-applicable values shall remain distinguishable from measured zero and negative findings.
Accessibility Parity: Manual and AI-assisted tasks shall satisfy applicable ACC-01 through ACC-53. Essential functionality shall not depend on a map, speech, precise gesture, or AI availability.
Configurable Definitions: Departments, permitted classifications, lifecycle policies, reporting definitions, and shared aliases shall be governed configurations, not incompatible hardcoded copies.
Given insufficient permission, when a direct API or AI action is requested, then it is denied without protected data disclosure and no state changes.
Given a stale record version, when an update executes, then the user receives a conflict and can preserve their input.
Given the same valid execution identifier submitted twice, then only one business effect occurs.
Given a failed save, then no success/received confirmation appears and valid input remains recoverable.
Authentication, Accounts, And Permissions: Business trace: BR-06, BR-10, BR-16.
Support sign-in, sign-out, session expiration, and access-denied handling.
Manage invitations, activation, suspension, and deactivation through an approved identity workflow; do not retain obsolete password forms unsupported by that workflow.
Assign approved responsibilities and record scopes; audit grants and revocations.
Store email, names, profile reference, identity reference, lifecycle state, and role grants.
Keep accounts separate from personnel records; preserve former staff history.
If public identity is included, provide accessible verification/recovery without treating a display reference as a secret.
A deactivated user's next protected action is denied according to the approved revocation policy.
A responder cannot grant administrator permissions or approve assessments without the corresponding grant.
Deactivation leaves historical actor references intact.
Mission Intake And Identification: Business trace: BR-02, BR-03, BR-06.
Create, view, update, and archive permitted mission records with immutable internal ID and unique human-readable reference.
Define draft-save, intake-save, and dispatch prerequisites separately; unknown information shall not be fabricated.
Capture source, caller name/contact/address/role/language, interpreter need, summary, conditions, type, subcategory, urgency, priority, and location.
Generate mission references safely under concurrent creation and retries; deleting/archiving a mission shall not cause reference reuse.
Record creator/updater from authenticated identity and enforce lock policy.
Preserve corrections and original intake provenance; priority changes require approved justification/confirmation.
Two simultaneous valid creations produce distinct references; a retry does not create a third record.
A missing dispatch prerequisite blocks dispatch but retains a permissible draft.
A locked mission rejects unauthorized edits through manual and command paths.
Mission Location And Geographic Awareness: Business trace: BR-01, BR-03, BR-15.
Store address components, unit, cross streets, landmarks, coordinates, source, precision/verification state, and verification time.
Support address suggestions, geocoding, reverse geocoding, and optional cross-street enrichment.
Permit manual text/landmark entry and approved approximate/unknown states; never use 0,0 as a missing-location substitute.
Display authorized mission, personnel, and assessment locations with text equivalents and distinct non-color-only meanings.
Identify stale personnel coordinates and device-permission failures.
Continuous location feeds and imagery shall have separately approved sourcing, accuracy, privacy, licensing, and outage rules.
Denied GPS permission or failed geocoding does not block a report with valid manual location information.
An unknown location remains unknown and is not plotted as a verified point.
A screen-reader user can enter/select location without using a map.
Hazards And Special Circumstances: Business trace: BR-03, BR-10, BR-14.
Capture mental-health crisis, violence, child/elder involvement, weapons, language barrier, hazmat, and medical emergency.
Support suicidal threats, missing/runaway concerns, utility risk, weather, public-health indicators, and prior-mission links where approved.
Distinguish reported, confirmed, corrected, and cleared hazard information.
Record source/actor/time and protect sensitive hazard fields.
Present critical hazards independently of general narrative.
An AI-suggested hazard is labeled unverified until staff accepts it.
Clearing a hazard preserves the original entry and reason.
Unauthorized users cannot obtain restricted behavioral-health details.
Personnel Directory And Availability: Business trace: BR-04, BR-10.
Maintain name, operational role, department, contact, skills, badge reference, optional account, location, and availability.
Search/filter recorded qualifications, department, status, and assignment.
Separate duty/availability/response semantics under approved definitions; audit changes.
Restrict self-update versus coordinator-update authority.
Deactivate/archive rather than lose assignment or badge history.
If certifications govern assignments, store verification and expiration and enforce approved eligibility rules.
Search for a skill returns only personnel with recorded matching qualifications.
Inactive personnel are excluded from new assignments unless a permitted exception is explicitly approved.
Off-duty changes apply the approved release policy rather than silently leaving conflicting mission assignments.
Assignments And Response Lifecycle: Business trace: BR-03, BR-04, BR-06, BR-15.
Support multiple personnel per mission with per-assignment status/history.
Update mission/personnel relationships atomically or with equivalent consistency guarantees.
Check duplicate assignments, commitments, qualification policy, and authorized overrides.
Enforce approved transitions across open, en_route, on_scene, cleared, and closed.
Record call received, dispatch, travel, arrival, transport start/end/destination, and clearing as applicable.
Do not infer en_route merely from assignment; record dispatch method separately from proof of delivery.
Support authorized release and reopening with reasons; closing does not erase deployment history.
Formal team/vehicle/equipment entities require approved scope rather than overloading personnel IDs.
Failed assignment leaves neither half of the relationship falsely updated.
Assigning a person does not create an arrival timestamp.
A conflicting commitment is blocked or shown for authorized override with reason.
Closure releases resources according to policy and preserves historical links.
Notes, People, Evidence, And Outcomes: Business trace: BR-03, BR-05, BR-06, BR-10.
Support call-taker, dispatcher, responder, supervisor, and follow-up narratives with attributable amendments.
Maintain one authoritative people-involved representation with role, name, gender if necessary, contact, address, injury, transport, and behavioral-health details.
Separate time-stamped events from editable summaries and restrict sensitive fields.
Support approved images/documents/media/bodycam/live-feed references with source, uploader, time, access, and retention.
Capture disposition, explanation, case reference, report-required/generated indicators, reviewer, and review time.
Validate closure prerequisites and preserve changes/removals under audit and retention rules.
Updating a summary does not replace original event history.
Restricted evidence cannot be downloaded using an unauthorized direct reference.
Closure with missing required disposition is rejected with an actionable error.
Mission History And Audit: Business trace: BR-06, BR-10.
Record creation, updates, status/priority changes, assignments, notes, decisions, closure/reopen, lock/unlock, and reversal.
Capture actor, event time, entry time, source, action, target, changes, and relevant execution ID.
Support authorized manual operational entries without allowing alteration of protected audit events.
Apply tamper resistance, retention, and audit-access restrictions.
Allow chronological reconstruction and authorized historical export with redaction rules.
A delayed entry preserves both occurrence time and time recorded.
Account deactivation does not remove actor attribution.
Undo creates a linked compensating/reversal event rather than deleting the original.
Situation Updates And Reminders: Business trace: BR-07, BR-15.
Store mission-linked reminder owner, due time, recurrence if approved, and active/overdue/completed/canceled state.
Support snooze, reset, cancel, acknowledge, and complete with actor/history.
Persist shared state beyond reload; distinguish an acknowledgment from a completed update.
Complete a reminder associated with an update only after that update persists.
Provide accessible overdue indicators; sound is optional and not the sole cue.
Escalation/external notification requires approved recipients, timing, delivery handling, and quiet-period policy where applicable.
Reloading or changing devices does not lose an authorized shared reminder.
A failed situation-update save leaves the reminder incomplete.
Two staff completing the same reminder do not create duplicate update effects.
Staff Damage Assessments: Business trace: BR-05, BR-06, BR-10.
Create/view/update assessments with date, disaster reference, property location, assessor, and contact.
Capture structure type, occupancy, primary residence, insurance, and unknown states.
Capture damage level/cause, roof/foundation observations, general description, and notes.
Capture utilities, access, immediate needs, displacement, estimate, and evidence through actual supported inputs.
Distinguish estimates from verified costs, public observations from field findings, and unknown from negative findings.
Preserve reassessment versions and link superseded findings.
Validate nonnegative counts/costs and approved severity guidance; reject invalid enumerations without losing input.
Zero displaced occupants and unknown occupant count remain distinguishable.
Reassessment retains prior observations and their provenance.
Uploaded evidence is associated with the correct assessment and restricted appropriately.
Public Damage Reporting: Business trace: BR-01, BR-05, BR-09, BR-10.
Accept valid public reports without a staff session.
Collect necessary reporter/contact/location/damage information with accessible guidance and valid unknown answers.
Explain privacy, emergency-response boundaries, and no assistance guarantee before submission.

Apply accessible anti-abuse and duplicate prevention without blocking legitimate assistive-technology users.
Keep public source and review status explicit; present approved public resources.
Status/correction, proxy submission, resume, and accommodation requests require approved identity/consent/privacy policies.
An unsigned resident can submit and receive a saved reference using only a keyboard or screen reader.
A network timeout followed by retry creates one report.
A public reference cannot retrieve another resident's private contact details.
A renter can use unknown owner-only information where permitted.
Assessment Review: Business trace: BR-05, BR-06, BR-08.
Represent submitted, under_review, needs_information, approved, rejected, duplicate, and superseded separately.
Record reviewer, decision time, reason, record version, and applicable evidence.
Support correction requests and resubmission with history.
Restrict decision authority and enforce approved self-review policy.
Re-review materially changed approved findings before including them in new official totals.
Link duplicates without deleting provenance or double-counting.
Rejecting a report yields rejected, not generic unapproved/pending.
An unauthorized assessor cannot approve their own report by an AI command or direct request.
Changed approved findings follow re-review and do not silently alter issued report snapshots.
Badges And Identification: Business trace: BR-11, BR-06.
Create identity documents linked to personnel with role, department, approved photo, template, and access label.
Store validity, active/revoked/expired/replaced state, issuance, and reprint history.
Treat badge access labels separately from account permission.
Produce genuine printable output and support actual photo capture/upload if included.
Integrate physical printing or scan verification only with supported devices/services and verified outcomes.
Distinguish generated, print-requested, print-confirmed, and failed; do not equate a database timestamp with physical success.
Generating a document does not mark physical print success.
Revocation remains visible to an approved verification workflow if implemented.
A QR/image is not the only accessible identification output.
Analytics And Exports: Business trace: BR-08, BR-10.
Compute mission, personnel, assessment, and badge metrics from approved shared definitions.
Support bounded period/timezone, type, priority, status, department, severity, and authorized search filters where relevant.
Include all supported damage categories and distinguish verified/unverified totals.
Produce trends and utilization using configured departments and declared formulas.
Match displayed and exported scope/totals; identify generation time, definitions, and exclusions.
Support CSV and accessible report output with correct quoting, safe treatment of spreadsheet formula-like input, pagination if needed, and redaction.
Response-time metrics depend on trustworthy milestone data; disclose incomplete records.
Closed missions are classified according to the agreed active definition, not legacy resolved text.
An affected assessment appears in the correct distribution category.
The same scope yields matching displayed/CSV/report totals and no unauthorized fields.
Official Situation Reports: Business trace: BR-08, BR-06.
Generate period/scope/cutoff-based drafts containing mission, priority, staffing, approved damage, and operational summaries.
Separate measured facts, staff judgments, and generated narrative; cite relevant sources.
Never hardcode normal/adequate/operational as an assessed condition.
Support review, approval, issuance, classification, and retained versioned snapshot.
Preserve previously issued values after later record changes; issue amendments rather than overwrite.
Export accessible approved content with author/reviewer, scope, generation/issuance times, and limitations.
Changing an assessment after issuance leaves the issued snapshot unchanged.
Unknown communications status is identified as unknown, not operational.
A generated draft does not become an official report without required review.
Public Assistance Resources: Business trace: BR-01, BR-09.
Maintain title, description, type, content/reference, thumbnail, category, ordering, ownership, and publication state.
Make published resources accessible without staff sign-in; keep drafts/private material restricted.
Support review date, expiration, removal from publication, and broken-link handling.
Provide accessible text/HTML or accessible documents for essential guidance.
Approved event/geography/need/language targeting shall not imply live availability or eligibility.
An unsigned resident can read a published resource but not its restricted draft.
Expired information is not silently presented as current.
Essential information remains available when an external PDF is inaccessible.
Interagency Contacts And Coordination: Business trace: BR-12, BR-06, BR-10.
Maintain agency/contact, contact methods, type, active state, verification time, and owner.
Restrict contact administration and private information access.
Record referral/communication attempt, recipient, channel, actor, time, purpose, and outcome.
Implement approved sending channels, acknowledgment, and follow-up separately from contact storage.
Record provider evidence where available and distinguish queued/sent/delivered/acknowledged/failed.
Selecting email as a channel does not show delivery without evidence.
A failed send can be retried safely without silent duplicate communication.
A partner receives only expressly authorized shared information.
Configuration, Guidance, And Usability: Business trace: BR-02, BR-16, BR-01.
Maintain system/organization name, contact information, approved branding, and themes.
Restrict mutations; separate publicly readable branding from private configuration.
Maintain accurate human-reviewed guidance, field definitions, examples, and known limitations.
Support accessible touch/keyboard input and validated themes.
Govern shared classifications, operational definitions, and alias changes with audit.
Multi-organization tenancy requires explicit isolation requirements; branding alone shall not imply it.
A signed-in non-admin cannot change protected settings.
Public branding retrieval does not disclose private service configuration.
Product help describes implemented behavior rather than nonexistent live tracking or printing.
Invocation And Input: Provide configurable non-conflicting shortcut and accessible touch/keyboard control, natural-language entry, deterministic shorthand, discoverable help, and approved aliases.
Context Resolution: Resolve authorized selected/referenced records, scope, timezone, and freshness. Ask for ambiguity rather than guess. Treat retrieved content as data, not executable instructions.

Action Contract: Each supported operation shall declare action name/version, argument schema, target/scoping rules, permission, prerequisites, confirmation class, side effects, idempotency behavior, result schema, and reversal policy.

Feature Coverage: Connect approved mission, personnel, assessment, reminder/report, resource/contact/badge, and administration actions to existing validated business operations as they are implemented.
Plan And Confirm: Distinguish questions/drafts/execution, resolve targets, show consequential diffs, and bind explicit confirmation to the plan, record versions, user, and scope.
Execution Consistency: Use atomic related changes where possible, stable execution IDs, bounded retries, and per-action partial-failure results.
Cancel And Reverse: Cancel before execution where possible; report completed effects honestly. Offer only supported safe reversal, preserving original/reversal history.
Unsaved And Bulk Work: Protect drafts, make bulk scope explicit, enforce batch/rate limits, and treat macros as individual governed actions.

Accessible Language And Fallback: Meet public accessibility, support approved languages, provide typed alternatives to optional dictation, and avoid automatic replay of stale consequential requests after reconnect.
Privacy And Audit: Minimize model context, govern history, preserve authenticated execution audit, and separate personal conversation removal from mandated record retention.
Progress And Measurement: Expose interpretation/execution progress, timeout, failure, and verified results; measure quality without unnecessary sensitive logs.
Ai Governance: Apply AI-01 through AI-12 below to every generated or executed operation.
Essential tasks remain manually completable.
Context is limited to the user's authorized data.
Generated, human-entered, and verified content are distinguishable.
Summaries identify supporting records and relevant times.
Missing information and uncertainty are explicit.
Consequential actions require applicable human confirmation.
Accepted changes and confirming user are audited.
Normal validation applies to generated data.
No fabricated hazards, credentials, damage findings, or operational status.
Provider failure does not disable intake, assignments, or status updates.
Provider retention and sensitive-data policy are approved before use.
Evaluation measures factual accuracy and omissions, not just fluency.
From an assessment task, an authorized dispatcher can request a mission assignment without first changing application context.
"Assign Alex" with two authorized matches requests clarification and performs no assignment.
A public user's request for private mission information is denied without revealing existence or content beyond approved policy.
Approval prepared for one report cannot be reused to approve a different report or changed version.
Revoking permission after preview blocks execution even if the user confirms.
Repeating the same valid action request produces one effect.
Failure on step two of a multi-step external workflow identifies completed step one and does not claim rollback.
"Undo that" reports an unavailable reversal for already delivered communication rather than pretending recall.
A command affecting an unsaved manual draft requests reconciliation instead of overwriting.
A malicious instruction embedded in a report does not change tool permissions or cause execution.
Screen-reader/keyboard users can invoke, clarify, confirm, cancel, and understand results.
AI outage leaves manual workflows and eligible deterministic commands usable; no stale dispatch replays automatically.
Target WCAG 2.2 AA; verify full tasks with automation and manual assistive-technology testing.
Provide semantic labels, meaningful alternatives, focus management, contrast, text enlargement/reflow, and non-map completion.
Support keyboard, touch, voice control, and alternative input without gesture-only or time-pressure dependencies.
Provide text alternatives, applicable captions/transcripts, and non-voice assistance.
Use plain language, minimal required input, unknown answers, error recovery, review, reduced motion, and non-AI help.
Translate complete tasks for approved languages; human-review critical guidance and retain original source text.
Support slow networks, permission denial, safe retry, shared-device privacy, and optional media loading.
Make consent, any authentication/anti-abuse, assisted reporting, and accommodation handling accessible and privacy-aware.
Publish accessible documents, confirmations, external-resource alternatives, and accessible optional AI.
Maintain accessibility support, known limitations, ownership, and remediation process.
Blind resident completes reporting, corrects validation errors, and reads confirmation without map use.
Low-vision user enlarges/reflows content without loss of controls or required information.
Limited-dexterity user completes without precise gestures or short time limits.
Deaf/non-speaking user receives essential guidance and support without audio-only/voice-only dependence.
A supported-language user receives translated errors, consent, and confirmation, not just introductory text.
Denied camera/GPS permissions do not block valid manual reporting.
Shared-device user can finish without private content being exposed to the next user.
Optional AI does not replace clear field guidance or require a conversation.
Proxy reporting, if approved, preserves helper/subject distinction and authorized follow-up boundaries.
Accessibility: Target WCAG 2.2 AA across released tasks and applicable generated content. Complete representative manual tests; do not claim legal certification.

Security: Use approved secure session/identity mechanisms, least privilege, input validation, protected file access, safe external references, and appropriate encryption in transit/at rest. Test object/field-level access and public enumeration.

Privacy And Retention: Approve field necessity, consent, role access, provider use, retention, export/redaction, and deletion/archive handling. Keep secrets and unnecessary personal data out of logs. Define conflict between deletion requests and mandatory records through approved policy.
Reliability: Define availability objectives and degraded operation. Essential intake and saves shall expose actual states; automatic retries shall be bounded and safe.
Backup And Restore: Define recovery point/time objectives, backup scope/retention, restore ownership, and tested restoration including attachments and relationships.
Performance And Capacity: Define concurrent staff/public users, mission/assessment volumes, evidence sizes, slow-network profile, and older devices.
Synchronization: Define permitted freshness/staleness windows and how cross-user updates propagate. Show last known state and prevent stale consequential execution.
Field/Offline Operation: If full offline entry is approved, specify encrypted local storage, retention, sync identity, conflict handling, and pending-versus-received distinction.
Internationalization: Support Unicode, language metadata, relevant scripts/direction, approved date/number formatting, and complete translated task content. Human-review critical guidance.
Observability: Measure save/command/integration failures, latency, conflicts, duplicate prevention, and audit completeness without sensitive prompt/content leakage. Define alert owners.
Maintainability: Use consistent shared definitions and validated business operations for manual, shorthand, and natural-language paths. Maintain approved documentation and action contracts.

Accessible Export Quality: Essential information shall not be available only as inaccessible scans, images, or QR codes. PDF exports require structure/reading-order verification; CSV is not a substitute for accessible narrative guidance.
Identity: sign-in/session/revocation/invitation supported by approved provider; fallback does not weaken access.
Mapping/geocoding: declared coverage, licensing, rate limits, privacy, ambiguous-match and outage behavior; manual alternative.
Evidence storage: protected access, supported upload, scanning/validation policy, retention, backup.
AI provider: approved context/retention, timeouts, quotas, supported languages, quality evaluation; manual/deterministic fallback.
Communications, conditional: real sending, safe retry, authenticated provider callbacks, delivery semantics, recipient/content confirmation.
Printing/verification, conditional: supported output/device protocol, attempt/result evidence, expired/revoked handling.
External CAD/vehicle tracking/partner feeds, conditional: separately approved contracts and reconciliation; not implied by data fields.
Inventory source records, relationships, enums, duplicates, evidence references, and retained audit information.
Approve mappings for legacy incident/mission naming, textual/numeric priorities, and legacy statuses.
Map approval booleans conservatively; false does not prove rejected. Preserve unknown legacy review semantics.
Preserve IDs/references where practical, or retain explicit crosswalks without reference reuse.
Reconcile mission/personnel assignments and quarantine inconsistent cases for human review.
Preserve sensitive access and attachment ownership; do not make private evidence public.
Validate counts, relationships, categories, timestamps, cost precision, and official snapshot meaning.
Rehearse migration, verify backup/restore, and define an approved cutover/recovery process.
Obtain operational sign-off on reconciled data and residual exceptions before using it as authoritative.

Accessible Authentication: If public accounts or report-status authentication are added, avoid memory or puzzle requirements without accessible alternatives.
Accessible Anti-Abuse Controls: Do not rely solely on image puzzles or audio challenges.
Clear Consent: Explain why information is collected and how it is used.
Assisted Reporting: If proxy reporting is enabled, distinguish the helper, affected person, and property representative.
Accommodation Requests: Consider an optional way to request accessible follow-up or a preferred communication method.
Emergency And Eligibility Clarity: Provide accessible, locally approved instructions for immediate emergencies.
Accessible Documents: Publish resources in accessible text or HTML where practical.
Accessible Confirmation Output: Make report references, summaries, and any downloadable receipts accessible.
Accessible External Resources: Review critical external resources for accessibility.
Optional Ai Assistance: Make AI interaction usable with keyboard, screen readers, voice control, and magnification.
Controlled Ai Output: Allow users to edit or reject generated text.
Application-Wide Availability: Make the command window available throughout supported application experiences.
Short-Key Invocation: Provide a configurable keyboard shortcut to open or focus the command window.
Shorthand Commands: Support concise commands alongside natural language.
Reusable Aliases: Allow approved aliases for frequently used commands, such as "brief" for a briefing draft.
No Required Ai Conversation: Allow deterministic shorthand to execute through the same validated action system without unnecessary model interpretation.
Explicit Context: Use authorized context such as the selected record, current task, and referenced identifiers.
Cross-Feature Commands: Support acting on a mission while the user is working with personnel, or drafting a report while reviewing assessments.
Ambiguity Handling: Ask a focused clarification when a person, mission, property, date, or scope is ambiguous.
Context Freshness: Refresh important record state before acting.
Temporal Context: Resolve relative dates and times using the configured organizational timezone.
User Input Versus Record Content: Treat report descriptions, attachments, external resources, and other users' notes as data, not instructions to the command system.
Action Catalog: Maintain an explicit catalog of supported actions, parameters, permissions, validation, and confirmation requirements.
Mission Actions: Search and summarize authorized missions.
Personnel Actions: Find personnel by recorded skills, department, or availability.
Damage-Assessment Actions: Create and update drafts.
Reporting And Reminder Actions: Draft summaries and situation reports.
Resource, Contact, And Badge Actions: Search published resources and authorized contacts.
Administrative Actions: Support authorized configuration and account operations only after their underlying workflows exist.
Public-Role Actions: Let public users draft or submit their own reports and find approved resources.

Permission Checks At Execution: Authenticate and authorize each action on the server.
Confirmation Policy: Read-only lookups and reversible drafting may execute without extra confirmation where permitted.
Validation: Use the same required fields, state transitions, assignment rules, and privacy controls as manual actions.
Atomic Operations And Partial Failure: Perform related database changes together where possible, including mission/personnel assignment updates.
Duplicate Prevention: Protect against repeated execution caused by double submission, retries, reconnects, or model/tool retries.
Verified Results: Show success only after the underlying operation confirms it.
Cancellation: Allow cancellation before execution.
Undo And Recovery: Offer undo for actions that can safely be reversed.
Unsaved Work: Do not silently overwrite a user's unsaved form changes.
Bulk And Repeated Actions: Define allowed batch sizes, rate limits, and role restrictions.
